What Plane Shapes (2-D Shapes) covers in CTET Paper I Maths

At the primary level this chapter blends content knowledge with pedagogy — how young children learn the idea. Expect questions on:

  • Naming 2-D shapes — circle, triangle, square, rectangle, oval and polygons
  • Counting sides and vertices (corners) of each shape
  • Telling curved boundaries from straight ones
  • Spotting shapes in everyday objects — the pedagogy CTET loves to test

Practise the full syllabus free on the CTET Paper I Mathematics course at vidaara.org, then test yourself here.

Key facts and formulas to remember

  • A polygon is a closed figure made only of straight line segments; a circle is not a polygon.
  • A triangle has 3 sides and 3 vertices; a square and a rectangle each have 4.
  • A square is a special rectangle with all four sides equal.
  • You need a minimum of 3 straight segments to enclose a region.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing a square with a rhombus, or a rectangle with a square.
  • Calling an oval a circle — an oval is an elongated closed curve.
  • Counting a circle as having "one side" instead of a single curved boundary.

quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper I – pattern questions on Plane Shapes (2-D Shapes). Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CTET Paper 1 Maths: Plane Shapes (2-D Shapes)

questions.q: How many sides does a square have?
A closed figure with 4 straight sides is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A polygon with 4 straight sides is a square.

questions.q: Which of the following 2-D shapes has 4 equal straight sides and 4 right-angled vertices?
questions.explanation: A square is a 2-D regular quadrilateral with 4 equal straight sides and 4 right angles.

questions.q: Which of the following geometric figures is a closed polygon with the minimum possible number of straight sides?
questions.explanation: A polygon is a closed 2-D figure formed by straight line segments. The minimum number of line segments required to enclose a 2-D region is 3, which forms a triangle.

questions.q: Which of the following shapes has no vertex?
questions.explanation: A circle has a curved boundary with no corners or vertices. A square, triangle and rectangle all have straight sides that meet to form vertices.

questions.q: Which of the following digits exhibits vertical line symmetry when written in standard block font?
questions.explanation: When drawn symmetrically in block font, the digit '8' can be split down the middle vertically so that the left side mirrors the right side.

questions.q: How many vertices (corners) does a pentagon have?
questions.explanation: A pentagon has 5 vertices — the same as its number of sides.

questions.q: A closed 2-D polygon has 7 straight sides and 7 corners. What is the name of this shape?
questions.explanation: A polygon bounded by 7 straight line segments having 7 interior angles and 7 vertices is a heptagon.

questions.q: Which geometric term describes a straight path that starts at a fixed point and extends endlessly in one direction?
questions.explanation: A ray has one fixed endpoint (origin) and continues infinitely in a single direction.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, each passing from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

faq.q: Are 2-D shape questions common in CTET Paper 1 Maths?
faq.a: Yes. Geometry — naming shapes, counting sides and vertices, and identifying shapes in real objects — is a regular part of the CTET Paper I Mathematics section, often mixed with a pedagogy angle.

faq.q: What is the difference between a side and a vertex?
faq.a: A side is a straight edge of a shape; a vertex (corner) is the point where two sides meet. A triangle has 3 of each.
No. A polygon is bounded only by straight sides. A circle has a single curved boundary, so it is not a polygon.
